column4: The source section's root ج-م-ع opens a local human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that wherever people are, God will bring them all together (جميعا). It makes the assembly universal across places.

The source section moves from a crowded human group to the day of gathering; this ayah says God will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers together in Hell (جامع المنافقين والكافرين). It gives the assembly a specifically punitive destination.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 10:28 gathers everyone, this ayah says each soul is tested for what it did and returned to God, its true Lord. It supplies the individual's reckoning within the gathered scene.

The source section connects the gathering day with the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says that on the day a witness is raised from every community. It shows the gathered multitude represented community by community.

The source section joins the جمع crowd to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says a witness is brought from every community and the Messenger is brought as witness over his people. It makes communal witnessing part of the assembly's judgment.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a mass of people, and its local scene is a military incursion; this ayah says Pharaoh sends gatherers into the cities to assemble his force. It shows a ruler deliberately collecting a crowd for confrontation.

The source section's جَمْع image is a human crowd met by an approaching force; this ayah describes the two groups coming into sight of each other (تراءى الجمعان) as Moses' people face Pharaoh's force. It supplies a direct encounter between assembled crowds.

The source section scales a small crowd up to the final gathering; this ayah commands that the wrongdoers, their counterparts, and what they worshipped be gathered and led to Hell. It specifies a judgment assembly grouped by its participants and deeds.

The source section brings the human crowd toward a day of gathering before its Lord; this ayah says people will dispute before their Lord on Resurrection Day. It adds open argument to the assembly's reckoning.

The source section's witness-root ش-ه-د and final gathering meet here: on that day the prophets and witnesses are brought, the record is set down, and judgment is made in truth. It specifies testimony and records within the assembled judgment.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for the day; after 39:69's public record and judgment, this ayah says every soul is repaid in full for what it did. It states the individual's outcome in that scene.

The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected on the final day; this ayah describes people as exposed before God with nothing hidden from Him. It states the exposure of what had been concealed.

The source section joins hidden contents to the day of account; after 40:16 exposes everyone, this ayah says each soul is repaid for what it earned and no injustice is done. It completes the exposure with its consequence.

The source section says the root ش-ه-د can name a gathering place and being present; this ayah names the day when the witnesses stand (يوم يقوم الأشهاد). It makes witnessing a public event of the final day.

The source section moves from a local human group to the final day; this ayah says that close friends become enemies to one another on that day, except the God-fearing. It marks how earthly group bonds can reverse when the assembly's true affiliations appear.

The source section says what lies in the breasts is collected; this ayah asks whether people with sickness in their hearts think God will not bring out their rancor (أضغانهم). It names a specific hidden content that becomes exposed.

The source section's final gathering is linked to the trumpet; this ayah says the trumpet is blown and calls the moment the promised day. It gives the summons immediately preceding the individual procession in 50:21.

The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د involves presence at the gathering; following the trumpet in 50:20, this ayah says every soul comes with a driver and a witness (سائق وشهيد). It makes each person's presence and testimony explicit.

The source section says what is hidden in the breasts is collected; after each soul arrives with a witness in 50:21, this ayah says the covering is removed and sight is sharp. It completes the arrival with the removal of concealment.

The source section moves from a people gathered as a local community to the last day; this ayah says relatives and children will not benefit people on Resurrection Day, when God judges between them. It marks the limit of kinship as support in the final assembly.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected and names 64:9 as the Day of Gathering; this ayah says God knows what people conceal and what they declare, and what is in breasts. It connects the gathering day in this surah with prior knowledge of the inner contents.

The source section pictures everyone collected on the final day; this ayah says people come to God individually (فرادى), stripped of what they had been given. It marks that universal assembly does not erase each person's solitary accounting.
The source section expands one crowd to humanity's final gathering; this ayah says every person comes to the Merciful individually (فردا). It marks the personal arrival within the universal day.

The source section's gathering day brings people before their Lord; after 18:47 gathers everyone and 18:48 presents them in rows, this ayah places the record and says it leaves nothing small or great uncounted. It supplies the detailed account confronting the assembly.

The source section links the gathering day to the witness-root ش-ه-د; this ayah says God will judge among the several religious communities on Resurrection Day and is witness over all things. It brings communities and divine witness into the same judgment scene.

The source section's root ش-ه-د names being present and bearing witness; this ayah has the descendants of Adam testify to God's lordship (شهدنا). It offers a collective witness-scene that contrasts with the final gathering: humanity's testimony begins before its worldly life.

The source section turns a small attacked crowd into humanity assembled on the final day; this ayah says a person flees from his brother. It begins a specific reversal in which the local ties of a crowd no longer hold.

The source section's local crowd is bound as a community; continuing the fleeing scene from 80:34, this ayah names a person's mother and father as those fled from. It extends the day-of-gathering reversal to the closest generational ties.

The source section moves from a local people to the universal day; continuing 80:34-35, this ayah names the spouse and children from whom a person flees. It extends the reversal from parentage to one's household.

The source section's gathering day brings everyone together; after 80:34-36 lists those a person flees, this ayah says each person has a concern that occupies him. It explains the individual urgency within the mass scene.

The source section pictures people gathered on a great day; this ayah shows the Spirit and angels standing in rows, with speech permitted only by the Merciful. It adds an ordered assembly and its limit on speech.

The source section scales a small crowd into the gathering of all people; this ayah names the day mankind stands before the Lord of the worlds. It states the universal assembly as a scene of standing before God.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names people collected for a day; this ayah calls the Day of Decision the appointed time for all together (أجمعين). It makes the day a common appointment for the whole multitude.

The source section says the witness-root ش-ه-د bears on a person's knowledge of his own conduct; this ayah tells each person to read the record, with himself sufficient as reckoner. It makes self-accounting a specific counterpart to the person's testimony.
The source section says what is in the breasts is collected for that day; this ayah says a person will be told what he sent ahead and left behind. It specifies what the day brings back into view.

The source section cites 45:28's gathered communities called to their records; this next ayah says those who believed and did good are admitted by their Lord into mercy. It gives one destination of the assembled communities.

The source section cites 45:28's universal summons to community records; this next ayah addresses the disbelievers and recalls that they acted arrogantly and were criminals. It gives the opposing outcome and the conduct it answers.

The source section explains the root ش-ه-د through witnessing and being present; this ayah says Jesus will be a witness over the People of the Book on Resurrection Day. It places a witness over a community in the final accounting.

The source section's whole-surah context includes the graves being overturned before the day; after people stream from graves in 36:51, this ayah records their question about who raised them from their resting place and the answer that the Merciful's promise is true. It completes the emergence scene with recognition of the summons.

The source section says the final day gathers people and exposes what is inside; this ayah says each soul comes pleading for itself and is repaid in full. It specifies the individual claim and recompense within the multitude.

The source section says what is in the breasts is collected on the day; this ayah says each soul will find the good and evil it did present before it. It gives a concrete disclosure of each person's record.
The source section moves from a local crowd to the great gathering day; this ayah says no close friend will ask another about his state. It marks the failure of social bonds amid the day’s assembly.

The source section takes a human crowd toward a universal day of accounting; this ayah says no soul can avail another on that day and that command belongs to God. It marks the boundary between being gathered together and being able to help one another.

The source section's root ج-م-ع names a human group and places horses amid it; this ayah tells the magicians to gather their plan and come in a row for their contest. It offers a specific, worldly gathering into formation before a confrontation.

The source section turns a human crowd toward the final gathering; this ayah says that on Resurrection Day people will disavow one another and curse the bonds they formed around idols. It shows a group's worldly attachments reversing at the day of account.
